title: Finite free completed coefficient extension is ordinary derived scalar extension
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $Y$ be any scheme. Work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/t^n)_Y$ and $S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}=\varprojlim_m(\mathcal O_L/v^m)_Y$ for the completed coefficient sheaves [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], where $(-)_Y$ is the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The inclusions of valuation rings give a canonical map $R\to S$. The $R$-module sheaf $S$ is finite free of rank $[L:E]$.

For $T=R,S$, write $D(T)$ for the derived category of sheaves of $T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K\in D(R)$ be derived $t$-complete [def-weil-derived-complete]. Form ordinary derived change of rings $K\otimes_R^L S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The reductions $S\to(\mathcal O_L/v^m)_Y$ induce the canonical completion map
$$
 \chi_{L/E,K}:K\otimes_R^L S\longrightarrow
 R\varprojlim_m\operatorname{Res}^L_m\bigl(K\otimes_R^L(\mathcal O_L/v^m)_Y\bigr)
 =K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L,
$$
Here $m\geq1$, $\operatorname{Res}^L_m$ is restriction of scalars along $S\to(\mathcal O_L/v^m)_Y$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and $R\varprojlim$ denotes the strict-tower cone model specified in [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], a derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit]. More explicitly, on a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] the compatible quotient maps $P\otimes_R S\to\operatorname{Res}^L_m(P\otimes_R(\mathcal O_L/v^m)_Y)$ define a map to the product killed strictly by $1-s$; the induced map to $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ has zero component in the shifted product. The map $\chi_{L/E,K}$ is the resulting morphism in $D(S)$, independent of the resolution. The last functor is exactly the strict-tower integral scalar extension of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and the right side is interpreted as its derived-limit realization [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]. This map is an isomorphism, natural in $K$, and $K\otimes_R^L S$ is derived $v$-complete. For $L=E$ it is the natural derived-completeness map $K\to R\varprojlim_n K\otimes_R^L(\mathcal O_E/t^n)_Y$, after the multiplication isomorphism $K\otimes_R^L R\cong K$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59 (completed coefficient sheaves); Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 3.4.12, pp. 22-23 (completed tensor and derived completeness); Proposition 3.5.1, p. 24 (completion as derived inverse limit). The finite-free coefficient-extension comparison is a consequence of these constructions, not a verbatim numbered lemma. Reduction of completed constant coefficients is Stacks Tag 093M, sites-modules.tex, lemma-completion-flat.

proof.text: Choose an integral basis of $\mathcal O_L$ over $\mathcal O_E$ of size $[L:E]$. Absolute-value uniqueness gives $|t|_L<1$; the DVR decomposition $t=u v^e$ thus has $e\geq1$. The adic basis-limit lemma gives the prescribed ring map $R\to S$ and $S\cong R^{\oplus[L:E]}$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), pp. 58-59: inverse limits of constant quotient sheaves. The basis and cofinal-filtration refinement below is an agent argument, not a numbered assertion of the source.

proof.text: The DVRs are Noetherian since their ideals are principal. The completed-constant theorem gives the canonical quotients $R/t^nR=(\mathcal O_E/t^n)_Y$, $S/v^mS=(\mathcal O_L/v^m)_Y$ and flatness over their constant DVR sheaves. Exact sheafification preserves injective uniformizer multiplication; tensoring these monomorphisms with the flat completions proves regularity of $t$ on $R$ and $v$ on $S$. Since $t=u v^e$, it is regular on $S$ too.

source.place: Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat: flat completion and canonical quotients; exact sheafification is Tag 03CN.

proof.text: Take a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ and put $Q=P\otimes_R S$, representing ordinary derived extension. Countable products are exact on the chosen small pro-etale skeleton. The derived-completeness hypothesis is exactly the quotient Roos triangle for $P$, using step 2. The regular quotient unit criterion thus makes $P$ locally $(t)$-complete.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul, one regular generator; canonical-unit refinement using the strict Roos comparison and Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 3.4.12.

proof.text: Finite free transport makes $Q$ locally $(t)$-complete over $S$. Unit-power invariance makes it locally $(v)$-complete. K-flat change of rings and the regular quotient criterion show that its specified $v$-quotient unit is invertible, and exhibit the quotient Roos triangle. Thus $Q$ is derived $v$-complete in the required sense.

source.place: Lemma 3.4.12, pp. 22-23; finite direct-sum calculation of the quotient-tower units, written here as a general ringed-site argument.

proof.text: Identify the quotient tower by $(p\otimes s)\otimes\bar z\mapsto p\otimes\bar s z$, with inverse $p\otimes\bar z\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes\bar z$. These formulas commute with differentials and transitions and carry the quotient units to the original coefficient reductions, with zero shifted component. Hence the unit of step 4 is precisely $\chi$. The scalar-augmentation descent lemma proves its derived naturality and representative independence; the integral-extension theorem identifies its target functor. For $L=E$, multiplication and that lemma identify it with the natural completeness unit. Different uniformizers of the same field generate the same powers of ideals.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10 and Proposition 3.5.1, pp. 22,24: completion via derived reduction towers. Explicit scalar augmentation and resolving-class descent are expanded here; not a verbatim assertion of the source.

lean.statement: theorem finiteFreeCompletedScalarComparison : Nonempty (((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars ((sheafCompose (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u (t + 1)} RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})).map (completedCoefficientMap l E L ι Y))).obj (SheafOfModules.unit (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l L Y))) ≅ ∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin (completedScalarRelativeDegree l E L ι) ↦ SheafOfModules.unit (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E Y)) ∧ (∀ K : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E Y), IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted l E Y K → IsIso ((completedScalarComparison l E L ι Y).app K) ∧ IsDerivedCompleteUnrestricted l L Y ((completedDerivedScalarExtension l E L ι Y).obj K)) ∧ ∀ P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).FullSubcategory, (completedScalarComparison l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) Y).app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj) ≫ (integralScalarExtensionComparisonOfUniverses l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) Y).hom.app P = completedScalarCounit l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) Y P.obj ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map ((completedScalarIdentityMultiplication l E Y).hom.app P.obj) ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map ((completedScalarIdentityUnit l E Y).app P.obj)
